confirmed: Source/version: no full text or markdown is on file (retrieval.json, c062: status=not_obtained). The complete OpenAlex abstract was read independently; the publisher full-text URL returned HTTP 403. No PDF, tables, or appendices were read, so source.version correctly identifies abstract-only evidence (OpenAlex W7162853600; https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17501229.2026.2678315).

Bibliographic metadata matches: title, Xiaoshuang Guo, Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching, published online 2026-05-30, and page span 1-21. Crossref supplies no abstract; OpenAlex marks the article closed access and lists no repository full text. The page span is metadata, not an inspected PDF page count (Crossref API /works/10.1080/17501229.2026.2678315, title/author/published-online/container-title/page; OpenAlex W7162853600, open_access).

Design: a controlled creative-writing experiment compares human-only, human–LLM collaborative, and LLM-only writing. Random assignment is not stated; design_class=other and criterion_1=unclear are appropriate. has_randomized_people_study=false means no randomized people study was confirmed from the available abstract, not that nonrandom assignment was established (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 2-4).

Counts: 40 Chinese undergraduate GFL students participated, each completing four writing tasks. These are people and tasks per person, not 40 texts or ratings. Randomized, analyzed, arm-specific, and total scored-output counts are not given; the form appropriately leaves those numerical fields null. At most 40 people could be analyzed in this reported experiment, below 50, supporting core=no and criterion_2=not_met (OpenAlex abstract, sentence 4).

Output scoring is established: the writings were evaluated with a Torrance-inspired rubric covering fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, supporting criterion_3=met. The scorer, exact rubric implementation, and analytical unit are not described (OpenAlex abstract, sentence 5).

Every quoted passage in S1-O1.reported, S1-O2.reported, and S1-O3.reported matches the independently reconstructed abstract verbatim. Collaborative writing has the highest reported creativity scores, particularly elaboration and originality; LLM-only writing has the lowest overall scores; human-only originality is described as comparable to collaborative originality (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 6-8).

No numerical outcome scores, effect sizes, intervals, test statistics, or p values are supplied. The form appropriately records no numerical statistics; comparable originality is qualitative and is not a reported equivalence test (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 6-8 and complete abstract).

Context classification ai_vs_human is supported for the human-only versus LLM-only output comparison, including the stated originality difference. The separate human–LLM versus human-only comparison concerns assistance; its assignment method remains unknown (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 3 and 7-8; creativity-codebook.md, sections 3-4).

This is an empirical experiment rather than a synthesis, so the empty synthesis fields are appropriate. The abstract mentions a risk of homogenization but supplies no scored across-person diversity outcome or diversity statistic (OpenAlex abstract, sentences 3-9).
summary: Only the OpenAlex abstract and Crossref metadata could be checked; random assignment is unreported, and the 40 participating students are below the core sample threshold. The form omits fluency and flexibility and overstates assignment details, study location, timing, and the originality comparison.
